$comment: Source of the external status checks (slo.ingest-availability, slo.dashboard-availability). `node ops/status/generate.ts` writes gatus/config.yaml and upptime/.upptimerc.yml from it; ops/status/test/status.test.ts checks both against this file and against docs/sla.md. Hostnames are deployment values, passed as environment variables.

ingest.sli: docs/sla.md §2.2: accepted within 2 seconds on one of the two ingest hostnames (one retry to the other). External checks cannot solve the proof-of-work, so they check the gateway's own health route, which answers 200 only while the node holds a snapshot, the current keys and a durable spool and is not draining (services/gateway/cmd/gateway/main.go).
ingest.combine: a vantage point records a slot good when at least one of the two hostnames passed (docs/sla.md §2.2)

dashboard.sli: docs/sla.md §2.2/§3.3: a journey step fails when it errors or takes longer than 3 s. External checks cover the two steps that need no sign-in: the portal's static origin, and the API behind it reaching the database (components.dashboards of the health endpoint, wire-formats §i.2).
dashboard.combine: a vantage point records a slot good when both checks passed

vantagePoints.where: GitHub-hosted runners: infrastructure we do not operate (C-30); feeds the public status page ORG/status (DV-06)
a small VPS at a provider that hosts nothing else of ours (ADR-0022 placement of Gatus; docs/sla.md §17 P7: the lean profile's second outside source)
the local probe on the application host (ops/README.md lean profile): the full canary-event SLI with proof-of-work and signed-in journeys, inside the failure domain
